- Heads-up for #314: `COMMUNITY_SUPPORT_EMAIL = 'Bradley@Bradleytgpcoaching.com'` will fail this guard on rebase. Import `SUPPORT_EMAIL` from `src/constants/support`, or add a reasoned allowlist entry if the owner keeps a separate safety contact.

AUDIT GPT-6.1 Sol — growth-project-mobile#324 @ 7f20255d681f6714a25fb9a97381d037dc84934f — VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

A/B/C: 0/1/0. Independent full T2 audit of all five changed files, PR contract, live comments and exact-head executed CI. The shared inbox, encoded subjects and source/retired-address guard are correct, but the advertised support/access recovery paths still fail silently when the email intent cannot open. [Candidate](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/commit/7f20255d681f6714a25fb9a97381d037dc84934f).

### B-324-1 — Must fix: the only email fallback can fail without telling the user or giving another working action

`src/screens/support/SupportInboxScreen.tsx:120-129` offers Email support when live chat is unavailable, but `Linking.openURL(...).catch(() => undefined)` swallows every launch rejection without any UI feedback; `src/screens/auth/CreateAccountScreen.tsx:1286-1297` returns the rejected email-intent promise without a handler, while the Request access label does not expose the address. Thus a device unable to open the mail intent gets no explanation/recovery from the first action and an unhandled rejection/no recovery from the second. This is inherited failure handling at the exact support entry points changed and claimed as working by this PR, not a defect in the new address constant. It violates the owner requirement that every failure say what happened and what the user can do next. [Support fallback:120-129](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/blob/7f20255d681f6714a25fb9a97381d037dc84934f/src/screens/support/SupportInboxScreen.tsx#L120-L129), [access request:1286-1297](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/blob/7f20255d681f6714a25fb9a97381d037dc84934f/src/screens/auth/CreateAccountScreen.tsx#L1286-L1297).

**Minimal fix:** handle the rejected intent at both callers (prefer one shared action), display specific calm copy such as “This device could not open an email app. Use the address below in your mail app or browser.”, expose the canonical address in selectable/copyable text and offer Retry; do not route back to the same unavailable chat or silently discard the rejection. Add rendered-caller regressions with `Linking.openURL.mockRejectedValue(...)` for both entry points, asserting visible actionable failure and no unhandled promise; preserve successful target/encoded-subject tests. The current changed support test only mocks a successful intent, so it does not cover this failure. [Current happy-path-only regression:20-29](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/blob/7f20255d681f6714a25fb9a97381d037dc84934f/src/screens/support/__tests__/SupportInboxUnavailable.test.tsx#L20-L29).

### Evidence / limits

All three required exact-head checks are SUCCESS; I read the test log and confirmed the support-email guard, unavailable-chat support test and CreateAccount suite executed and passed (overall 395 suites / 5,351 tests). Those happy-path passes do not close B-324-1. No local heavy tests were run for this read-only audit; the finding follows directly from the two rejection handlers and their missing failure assertions. [Executed Typecheck/lint/test](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/actions/runs/36942228568/job/110636151831), [Actions analysis](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/actions/runs/36942228595/job/110636152218), [JS/TS analysis](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/actions/runs/36942228595/job/110636151985).

The separate community/policy/error-mapper changes must preserve the single support constant on integration; no new optional finding is counted for that already-recorded dependency. [PR integration scope](https://github.com/BradleyGleavePortfolio/growth-project-mobile/pull/324).
